title: RBAC v2 event shaping and canonical SIEM export spec v1.0
body:
Working draft: concise guide for shaping RBAC v2-derived audit events into a canonical SIEM export payload. Purpose: reduce downstream parsing complexity, preserve RBAC intent, and enable safe schema evolution with clear rollback steps.

Context and motivation:
- RBAC v2 introduces richer role tuples (role_id, scope, constraints, grant_type) and ephemeral grants. SIEM consumers (SecOps, SOC tools) expect stable flattened fields.
- We need a canonical export shape that: preserves necessary semantics for investigations, keeps row size predictable for SIEM ingestion, and is backwards-compatible for 12+ months.
- This doc is a technical shaping spec + versioning checklist focused on mapping, sampling, and migration playbook.

Non-goals:
- Not a full event taxonomy reference (see TAX-APPENDIX). Not prescribing retention policies.

Key design principles:
1) Always include a minimal core (event envelope) that never changes semantics: event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, actor_id, outcome.
2) Prefer typed, short top-level fields rather than long nested blobs for SIEM performance. Use namespacing for RBAC-specific extras (rbac_*).
3) Provide both flattened fields for common queries and an optional payload_blob for fidelity when needed.
4) Version field required: schema_version (semantic: v1.0, v1.1, v2.0).
5) Deprecation window: 12 months + 1 release cycle.

Canonical export shape (recommended top-level fields) — textual table follows (flattened):
- schema_version: string (e.g., v1.0)
- event_id: string (uuid)
- detected_at: rfc3339 timestamp (when exported)
- event_time: rfc3339 timestamp (when action happened)
- tenant_id: string
- actor_id: string (primary principal id)
- actor_type: string (user|service|machine)
- actor_principal: string (email or service name when available)
- outcome: string (allowed|denied|error|escalated)
- action: string (canonical action name e.g., session.create, role.grant, token.exchange)
- resource_id: string (canonicalized resource path)
- resource_type: string (model, deployment, project, dataset)
- auth_decision_reason: string (brief code; map to deterministic codes)
- rbac_effective_roles: string (comma-separated stable role ids at time of event)
- rbac_grants_delta: string (if RBAC change event; JSON-stringified short blob)
- rbac_policy_snapshot_ref: string (optional, pointer to policy snapshot id)
- evidence_links: string (comma-separated short ids to evidence artifacts)
- export_tags: string (comma list; e.g. sampled:true,priority:high)
- payload_blob: string (optional base64 or compressed JSON for full fidelity)

Notes on rbac_grants_delta and payload_blob:
- rbac_grants_delta should be a small, predictable element summarizing change: e.g. +role:billing:project:proj-123; -role:reader:deployment:dep-987. Keep length < 2k chars.
- payload_blob reserved for full audit event when downstream needs to rehydrate state; include compression and base64 to keep SIEM parsers from exploding on nested JSON.

Field mapping rules from RBAC v2 to canonical fields (guidelines):
- actor_id: pick the authoritative principal id (primary sub field). If ephemeral key present, map both actor_id and actor_principal (principal carries human-friendly).
- rbac_effective_roles: compute after the auth decision, resolved at the moment of action (post-evaluation). Include stable role IDs, not display names.
- action: normalize using the Action Vocabulary (see ACTION-VOCAB v1). For RBAC change events use canonical verbs: role.assign, role.revoke, policy.update, policy.rollback.
- resource_id: prefer platform-canonical resource URIs (/projects/{}/deployments/{}), not free text.

Sampling, batching and export sizing guidance:
- For high-volume ready-only events (e.g., token_validation success), enable sampled export by default with deterministic sampling key: sha256(tenant_id + actor_id) % N. Sample rates configurable per tenant.
- Always export 100% for: role changes, policy updates, authorization failures (denied), and any event with outcome != allowed.
- If payload_blob is present, tag export_tags with sampled:false and payload:true.

Versioning and compatibility rules:
- Schema_version bump rules:
  * patch (v1.0 -> v1.0.1): non-breaking text clarifications, enumerations extended with new values in a documented allowlist.
  * minor (v1.0 -> v1.1): additive non-breaking fields added (new optional fields). Receivers must ignore unknown optional fields.
  * major (v1.x -> v2.0): breaking changes (rename required fields, remove fields, change types). Major bumps require migration window: announce 90 days prior, dual-writing for 60 days, consumer opt-in test harness.
- Deprecation markers: add deprecated_field list in metadata with removal target date.

Migration checklist (to roll a new minor/major export schema):
1) Draft spec and compatibility matrix + example events.
2) Publish on CONFLUENCE with changelog and semantic version.
3) Notify consumers (integrations slack, sec-ops mailing list) with example payloads and parsing guidance.
4) Start test-only export to staging SIEM endpoint (dual-write flag).
5) Monitor error rates and parsing failures for 14 days.
6) Flip to production dual-write (both old and new) for 60 days.
7) After acceptance, remove dual-write and mark old schema deprecated with timeline.
8) After deprecation window, remove fields server-side with a major bump if necessary.

Rollback playbook (if downstream parsing breaks upon release):
- Immediate action: enable routing to the legacy export stream (feature flag) and pause new schema rollouts.
- Postmortem: capture sample broken events, identify diff with old schema, create hotfix patch (patch/minor as allowed), and re-run dual-write with consumer acceptance.

Testing and validation matrix (baseline automation):
- Unit tests: schema validation and canonicalizer for 100% of action types.
- Integration tests: ingest sample events into a mock SIEM and assert field presence and types.
- Consumer contract tests: a small CI job consumers can run to validate they can parse new optional fields.
- Fuzzing: random RBAC tuples fed to canonicalizer; ensure payload_blob not exceeding size threshold (configurable, default 64KB).

Example transformed events (textual):
1) Successful auth check (sampled):
{
  "schema_version": "v1.0",
  "event_id": "e-9a7f...",
  "detected_at": "2026-02-26T15:20:11Z",
  "event_time": "2026-02-26T15:20:11Z",
  "tenant_id": "acme",
  "actor_id": "usr-1234",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "actor_principal": "alice@acme.com",
  "outcome": "allowed",
  "action": "model.invoke",
  "resource_id": "/projects/proj-12/deployments/dep-9",
  "resource_type": "deployment",
  "rbac_effective_roles": "role:reader:proj-12",
  "export_tags": "sampled:true",
  "payload_blob": "",
}

2) Role grant event (always exported):
{
  "schema_version": "v1.0",
  "event_id": "e-a1b2...",
  "detected_at": "2026-02-26T15:21:02Z",
  "event_time": "2026-02-26T15:21:02Z",
  "tenant_id": "acme",
  "actor_id": "svc-deploy-bot",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "actor_principal": "redwood-deploy-bot",
  "outcome": "allowed",
  "action": "role.assign",
  "resource_id": "project:proj-12",
  "resource_type": "project",
  "rbac_grants_delta": "+role:editor:project:proj-12",
  "rbac_policy_snapshot_ref": "policy-snap-2026-02-26-8",
  "export_tags": "sampled:false,payload:false",
  "payload_blob": "",
}

Operational notes and open questions:
- Q1: payload_blob encoding preference: base64+gzip vs ndjson raw? Proposal: base64(gzip(json)) to avoid line-breaking in SIEM.
- Q2: How to indicate ephemeral grants that are ephemeral TTL-based? Include grant_type:ephemeral in rbac_grants_delta.
- Q3: Downstream cost: SIEM ingestion has tokenized cost per field. Consider a trimmed canonical view for customers on low tiers.

Action items (next steps):
- Owners: Maya to publish spec on CONFLUENCE and link to exporter PR.
- Omar to add unit tests for canonicalizer and size checks.
- Priya to coordinate notification cadence with SecOps.

Appendix (short references):
- ACTION-VOCAB v1 (internal link)
- POLICY-SNAPSHOT-SPECS (internal link)
- SIEM-INGEST-REQUIREMENTS (list of partner constraints)

Open: this is a working draft — expect iterative changes. If you are a SIEM consumer, please add parsing constraints to JIRA-AUDIT-312.
